title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a deployed tool carrying hidden functionality that its users were not told about. The markers were embedded in the system prompt Claude Code sends to the model, and they activated only under specific conditions: a custom API base URL combined with particular timezones or hostnames. For anyone running the tool in its default configuration the code stayed dormant, which is why it could persist unnoticed. The failure sits at the boundary between a vendor's internal detection interests and the transparency owed to the people running the software.

The mechanism was obfuscated rather than documented. Domain and keyword lists were stored as base64 strings decoded with an XOR key, and the output changed in ways, an apostrophe character and a date separator, that would not look wrong to anyone reading a prompt. Catching this would have required either inspecting the binary and decoding the strings, or noticing the prompt text shifting with timezone and hostname. Neither is a normal part of using a coding assistant.

What is not established is Anthropic's intent. The reporting describes the feature as an experiment and attributes that characterization to the company, and the claim that it targeted resellers, unauthorized gateways, and distillation pipelines comes from the blog author's assessment rather than from a finding. Alibaba's reported ban rests on a source, and the underlying allegation of backdoor risk has not been adjudicated.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A blog post reports that Claude Code version 2.1.196 contains hidden markers in the system prompt it sends to the model. The code changes the apostrophe in the phrase about today's date and swaps dashes for slashes in the date itself, depending on the user's timezone and the API base URL. The trigger is the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL setting. Timezones Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi change the date format, and hostnames matching a hidden list of Chinese company, AI lab, and proxy domains change the apostrophe character.

The domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings decoded with an XOR key. The author says the feature likely targets resellers, unauthorized gateways, and distillation pipelines, but calls the hidden approach a strange choice for a tool asking for trust. For most users the code stays inactive, since it only runs when a custom base URL is set. The article notes the bypass is trivial, through changing the hostname, timezone, or patching the binary.
